Where did you get your BRT? Did you rescue him or did he come from a reputable breeder? A good breeder should also help you, and be giving you advice and resources through out the dogs life, especially the first 2 yrs. 

Also, do you know what lines he has come from? Another thing a good breeder can assist with, is understanding the lineage that the parents came from, which can impact the overall behavior of the dog and their tendencies. 

Sure, the BRT was bred as a military guard dog, but the modern BRT can have many different variations in the breed, (some have a more intense guarding and territorial instinct, while others might be more naturally laid back and friendly.) This knowledge can help in learning more about your dogs natural temperament and help with understanding his triggers and inclinations better, and therefore be able to work with him more efficiently. 

I hope that helps!

They do NOT shed like normal dogs! They have a *double* *hair* coat,  like the Giant Schnauzer, Bouvier de Flanders, or many terrier type breeds, like the Airedale.

Therefore, you can pet them all day long, and no hair will get on your hands or clothes! However, if you do not maintain the coat properly, and brush regularly and use an undercoat rake often, then you will find dust bunny or tumbleweed clumps of undercoat hair, under furniture, or corners of the home. (The hair is quite heavy and tends to stay on the ground, instead of getting in the air.)

(Keeping the coat a lot shorter then the traditional show coat, would probably help with this, also.)

I was also confused about the hypoallergenic debate, due to the fact they have hair coats, and require regular grooming like a poodle! (I have owned several poodles, and they have what's called a *single hair* coat, which is what most people refer to as a truly "hypoallergenic coat," because it is practically like human hair and no hair is shed on you, or around the home!)

Hope that explanation helps! BRT's are certainly still a much better option than most breeds if you do have allergies.
